title.zh: 卷八十八 列傳第七十六: 隱逸
title.raw: 卷八十八 列傳第七十六: 隱逸 Volume 88 Biographies 76: Recluses

sentences.zh: 眭誇 馮亮 鄭修 崔廓 子賾 徐則 張文詡

translations.literal: Suikua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, his son Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu
translations.idiomatic: Suikua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, Cui Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu

sentences.zh: 蓋兼濟獨善，顯晦之殊，其事不同，由來久矣。

translations.literal: For benefiting all and cultivating oneself alone, the difference between public service and withdrawal—their affairs are not the same, and this has been so from long ago.
translations.idiomatic: The choice between benefiting the world and perfecting oneself alone, between serving in the open and withdrawing into obscurity—these paths have differed from the earliest times.

sentences.zh: 昔夷、齊獲全于周武，華矞不容于太公，何哉？

translations.literal: In former times Boyi and Shuqi were preserved whole by King Wu of Zhou, while Hua Yu was not tolerated by Grand Duke Jiang—why?
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Boyi and Shuqi were spared by King Wu of Zhou, yet Hua Yu found no place with the Grand Duke Jiang—why was that?

sentences.zh: 求其心者，許以激貪之用；

translations.literal: Those who sought their hearts praised them as useful for restraining greed;
translations.idiomatic: Those who looked to their inner purpose hailed them as a check on greed;

sentences.zh: 督其跡者，矯以教義之風。

translations.literal: those who scrutinized their conduct corrected by them with a wind of teaching righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: those who judged them by their deeds took them as a corrective wind of moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 而肥遁不歸，代有其人矣。

translations.literal: Yet those who concealed themselves and did not return—each age has had such men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in every generation there have been men who withdrew deep into hiding and never came back.

sentences.zh: 故《易》稱「遁世無悶」，「不事王侯」。

translations.literal: Thus the Book of Changes says, 'One who withdraws from the world is without vexation' and 'does not serve kings and lords.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Book of Changes speaks of one who 'leaves the world behind without distress' and 'serves neither kings nor lords.'

sentences.zh: 《詩》云「皎皎白駒，在彼空谷」。

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'The bright white colt is there in that empty valley.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes has it: 'Bright is the white colt, there in the empty valley.'

sentences.zh: 《禮》云「儒有上不臣天子，下不事諸侯」。

translations.literal: The Rituals says, 'There are scholars who above do not serve the Son of Heaven as subjects, and below do not serve feudal lords.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites declares that some scholars 'will not bow to the Son of Heaven above, nor serve the feudal lords below.'

sentences.zh: 《語》曰「舉逸民，天下之人歸心焉」。

translations.literal: The Analects says, 'Raise up reclusive subjects, and the people throughout the realm will turn their hearts to you.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says that when reclusive worthies are brought forward, 'the hearts of the people throughout the realm will incline toward you.'

sentences.zh: 雖出處殊途，語默異用，各言其志，皆君子之道也。

translations.literal: Though whether to serve or withdraw follows different paths, and speech and silence serve different ends, each expresses his purpose—all are the way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Though whether to enter public life or withdraw, to speak or keep silent, follows different courses, each man declares his own intent—and all alike belong to the way of the gentleman.

sentences.zh: 洪崖兆其始，箕山扇其風，七人作乎周年，四皓光乎漢日。

translations.literal: Hong Ya inaugurated it at the beginning; Mount Ji fanned the breeze; the Seven Worthies arose in the years of Zhou; the Four Hoary Heads shone in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Ya opened the way at the beginning, Mount Ji spread the example, the Seven Worthies appeared in Zhou times, and the Four Hoary Heads shone in the Han.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以降，其流逾廣。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, this current grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward, the movement spread ever wider.

sentences.zh: 其大者則輕天下，細萬物；

translations.literal: The greater among them looked lightly upon the realm and made little of all things;
translations.idiomatic: The greater ones held the realm lightly and regarded all things as insignificant;

sentences.zh: 其小者則安苦節，甘賤貧。

translations.literal: the lesser found peace in stern integrity and were content with lowly poverty.
translations.idiomatic: the lesser ones found peace in austere integrity and were content with humble poverty.

sentences.zh: 或與世同塵，隨波瀾以俱逝；

translations.literal: Some mingled with the world, drifting with the waves to pass away together;
translations.idiomatic: Some mingled with the world and drifted away with the tide;

sentences.zh: 或違時矯俗，望江湖而獨往。

translations.literal: some defied the times and corrected custom, gazing toward rivers and lakes to walk alone.
translations.idiomatic: others defied their age and corrected its ways, turning toward rivers and lakes to walk alone.

sentences.zh: 狎玩魚鳥，左右琴書，拾遺粒而織落毛，飲石泉而庇松柏。

translations.literal: They played with fish and birds, kept zithers and books at hand, gathered fallen grain and wove fallen feathers, drank from stone springs and took shelter under pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: They amused themselves with fish and birds, kept lutes and books close at hand, gathered fallen grain and wove shed feathers, drank from stone springs, and sheltered beneath pines and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 放情宇宙之外，自足懷抱之中。

translations.literal: They released their passions beyond the cosmos and found sufficiency within their own hearts.
translations.idiomatic: They gave free rein to feeling beyond the bounds of the universe and found contentment within their own hearts.

sentences.zh: 然皆欣欣於獨善，鮮汲汲於兼濟。

translations.literal: Yet all rejoiced in self-cultivation alone and rarely strove eagerly to benefit all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all alike took joy in perfecting themselves alone and seldom strove with urgency to benefit the wider world.

sentences.zh: 夷情得喪，忘懷累有。

translations.literal: They set aside attachment to gain and loss and forgot the burdens they carried.
translations.idiomatic: They set aside concern for gain and loss and cast off the burdens that weigh upon others.

sentences.zh: 比夫邁德弘道，匡俗庇人，可得而小，不可得而忽也。

translations.literal: Compared with those who advance virtue and broaden the Way, who reform custom and shelter the people, these may seem small and can be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with those who advance virtue, broaden the Way, reform custom, and shelter the people, such men may seem lesser—but they cannot be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 而受命哲王，守文令主，莫不束帛交馳，蒲輪結轍，奔走岩穀，唯恐不逮者，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet every sage king receiving the mandate and every cultured sovereign who preserved the tradition sent gifts and dispatched carriages rushing to mountain caves, fearing they might not arrive in time—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet sage kings who received the mandate and cultured rulers who upheld the tradition all sent gifts and dispatched rush-wheeled carriages to mountain valleys, racing lest they arrive too late—why?

sentences.zh: 以其道雖未弘，志不可奪，縱無舟楫之功，終有堅貞之操，足以立懦夫之志，息貪競之風。

translations.literal: Because though their Way had not yet spread widely, their purpose could not be wrested away; though they had no achievement as boat or oar for the realm, they possessed steadfast integrity that could rouse the spirit of the weak-hearted and still the wind of greedy struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Because though their teaching had not yet spread far, their resolve could not be broken; though they had no achievement as helmsmen of state, their steadfast integrity could steel the timid and quell the wind of greedy rivalry.

sentences.zh: 與苟得之徒，不可同年共日，所謂無用以為用，無為而無不為也。

translations.literal: They could not be placed on the same day or year as those who grasped only what they could get—the useless made useful, doing nothing yet leaving nothing undone.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot be compared with those who seize whatever they can—the useless made useful, acting without acting, and thereby leaving nothing undone.

sentences.zh: 自叔世澆浮，淳風殆盡，錐刀之末，競入成群。

translations.literal: From the decadent age downward, the pure wind nearly expired, and even the tip of an awl became a prize people raced after in crowds.
translations.idiomatic: Since the decadent age, the pure wind has nearly vanished, and men scramble in crowds even over the point of an awl.

sentences.zh: 而能冥心物表，介然離俗，望古獨適，求友千齡，亦異人矣！

translations.literal: Yet those who could darken their minds beyond the surface of things, stand apart from the vulgar, look to antiquity in solitary fittingness, and seek friends across a thousand ages—these were extraordinary people!
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who could still fix their minds beyond the world of things, stand cleanly apart from the vulgar, look to antiquity in solitary contentment, and seek companions across a thousand years—such men were truly extraordinary!

sentences.zh: 何必御霞乘雲而追日月，窮極天地，始為超遠哉！

translations.literal: Why must one ride clouds to pursue sun and moon, reach the ends of heaven and earth, before one is deemed transcendent and far?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one ride the clouds and chase the sun and moon, reaching the utter ends of heaven and earth, before one is counted truly transcendent?

sentences.zh: 案《魏書》列眭誇、馮亮、李謐、鄭脩為《逸士傳》。

translations.literal: According to the History of Wei, Suikua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu are listed in the 'Biographies of Hermits.'
translations.idiomatic: The History of Wei lists Suikua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu in its 'Biographies of Hermits.'

sentences.zh: 《隋書》列李士謙、崔廓、廓子賾、徐則、張文詡為《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: The History of Sui lists Li Shiqian, Cui Kuo, Kuo's son Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu in the 'Biographies of Recluses.'
translations.idiomatic: The History of Sui lists Li Shiqian, Cui Kuo, Cui Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu in its 'Biographies of Recluses.'

sentences.zh: 今以李謐、士謙附其家傳，其餘並編附篇，以備《隱逸傳》云。

translations.literal: Now Li Mi and Li Shiqian are placed with their family biographies; the rest are compiled in this chapter to complete the 'Biographies of Recluses.'
translations.idiomatic: Here Li Mi and Li Shiqian are placed with their family biographies, while the rest are gathered in this chapter to complete the 'Biographies of Recluses.'

sentences.zh: 眭誇，一名旭，趙郡高邑人也。

translations.literal: Suikua, also named Xu, was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Suikua, also called Xu, was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邁，晉東海王越軍謀掾，後沒石勒，為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mai was military strategist to Prince of Donghai Sima Yue of Jin; later he fell to Shi Le and became Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mai had been military strategist to Prince of Donghai Sima Yue of Jin; later, after falling into Shi Le's hands, he became Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父邃，字懷道，慕容寶中書令。

translations.literal: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, was Director of the Secretariat under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, served Murong Bao as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 誇少有大度，不拘小節，耽好書傳，未曾以世務經心。

translations.literal: Suikua from youth possessed great breadth of spirit, paid no heed to minor matters, devoted himself to books and records, and never once allowed worldly affairs to occupy his mind.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Suikua had a generous spirit, cared little for petty conventions, loved books and records, and never let worldly affairs weigh on his mind.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，浩然物表。

translations.literal: He loved wine and lived with carefree detachment above the mundane world.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and lived with an expansive ease above the affairs of the world.

sentences.zh: 年三十，遭父喪，須鬢致白，每一悲哭，聞者為之流涕。

translations.literal: At thirty he suffered his father's death; his beard and temples turned white, and each time he wept in grief those who heard were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he lost his father; his beard and temples turned white, and each time he wept in grief those who heard him were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 高尚不仕，寄情丘壑。

translations.literal: Holding himself in lofty abstention from office, he entrusted his feelings to hills and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself aloof from office and gave his heart to hills and ravines.

sentences.zh: 同郡李順願與之交，誇拒而不許。

translations.literal: Li Shun of the same commandery wished to befriend him, but Suikua refused and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun of the same commandery wished to befriend him, but Suikua refused.

sentences.zh: 邦國少長莫不憚之。

translations.literal: Young and old throughout the state all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old throughout the district stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 少與崔浩為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: In youth he was the closest of friends with Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Cui Hao were the closest of friends.

sentences.zh: 浩為司徒，奏徵為中郎，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: When Hao became Minister Over the Masses he memorialized to summon Suikua as Gentlemen of the Palace, but Suikua pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao became Minister Over the Masses, he memorialized to summon Suikua as Palace Gentleman, but Suikua pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 州郡逼遣，不得已，入京都，與浩相見。

translations.literal: Pressed by prefecture and commandery he had no choice but to enter the capital and meet Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the prefecture and commandery, he had no choice but to enter the capital and see Hao.

sentences.zh: 經留數日，唯飲酒談敘平生，不及世利。

translations.literal: He stayed several days, drinking wine and conversing on life past, never touching worldly profit.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed several days, drinking wine and talking over their lives together, never touching worldly gain.

sentences.zh: 浩每欲論屈之，竟不能發言，其見敬憚如此。

translations.literal: Hao always wished to argue and bend him but could never get the words out—such was the respect and awe in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Hao always meant to argue him into submission, yet could never bring himself to speak—such was the respect and awe he inspired.

sentences.zh: 浩後遂投詔書於誇懷，亦不開口。

translations.literal: Later Hao thrust the edict into Suikua's bosom, but Suikua still did not open his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hao thrust the edict into Suikua's bosom, but Suikua still would not speak.

sentences.zh: 誇曰：「桃簡，卿已為司徒，何足以此勞國士也？

translations.literal: Suikua said, 'Taojian, you are already Minister Over the Masses—why trouble a man of the realm with this?
translations.idiomatic: Suikua said, 'Taojian, you are already Minister Over the Masses—why bother a man of the realm with this?

sentences.zh: 吾便將別。」

translations.literal: I shall take my leave.'
translations.idiomatic: I shall take my leave now.'

sentences.zh: 桃簡，浩小名。

translations.literal: Taojian was Hao's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Taojian was Hao's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 浩慮誇即還，時乘一騾，更無兼騎，乃以誇騾內之廄中，冀相維縶。

translations.literal: Fearing Suikua would at once return—he had only one mule and no spare mount—Hao stabled Suikua's mule in his own stable, hoping to hold him there.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Suikua would leave at once—he had only one mule and no second mount—Hao stabled Suikua's mule in his own stable, hoping to keep him there.

sentences.zh: 誇遂托鄉人輸租者，謬為御車，乃得出關。

translations.literal: Suikua then had a fellow townsman who delivered rent pretend to drive the cart and thus got out through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Suikua then had a fellow townsman who was delivering rent grain pretend to drive the cart, and in that way got out through the pass.

sentences.zh: 浩知而歎曰：「眭誇獨行士，本不應以小職辱之，又使其人杖策復路，吾當何辭以謝也！」

translations.literal: When Hao learned of it he sighed and said, 'Suikua is a man who walks alone—he should never have been insulted with a small post, and to make the man walk staff in hand on the road again—what words can I offer in apology!'
translations.idiomatic: When Hao learned of it he sighed and said, 'Suikua is a man who walks his own path—I should never have insulted him with a petty post, and now to make him walk staff in hand on the road again—what apology can I possibly offer!'

sentences.zh: 時朝法甚峻，誇既私還，將有私歸之咎。

translations.literal: The court law was then very severe; since Suikua had returned privately he would have faced punishment for unauthorized departure.
translations.idiomatic: The court law was then very strict, and since Suikua had returned without permission he would have faced punishment for unauthorized departure.

sentences.zh: 浩仍相左右，始得無坐。

translations.literal: Hao still sided with him on both sides, so he finally escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao continued to support him on every side, and in the end Suikua escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 經年，送誇本騾，兼遺以所乘馬，為書謝之。

translations.literal: After a year Hao sent back Suikua's original mule along with the horse he himself had ridden, with a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Hao sent back Suikua's original mule, together with the horse he himself had ridden, and wrote a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 誇更不受其騾馬，亦不復書。

translations.literal: Suikua again refused the mule and horse and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Suikua again refused the mule and horse and did not write back.

sentences.zh: 及浩沒，為之素服，受鄉人弔唁，經一時乃止。

translations.literal: When Hao died Suikua wore unhemmed mourning and accepted condolences from fellow townspeople, continuing for a time before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao died, Suikua wore unhemmed mourning and accepted condolences from fellow townspeople, continuing for a time before he stopped.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「崔公既死，誰能更容眭誇！」

translations.literal: He sighed and said, 'Now that Lord Cui is dead, who can still tolerate Suikua!'
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, 'Now that Lord Cui is dead, who will still tolerate Suikua!'

sentences.zh: 婦父巨鹿魏攀，當時名達之士，未嘗備婿之禮，情同朋好。

translations.literal: His wife's father Wei Pan of Julu, a renowned man of the age, never performed full rites toward a son-in-law—their affection was like that of friends.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's father Wei Pan of Julu, a celebrated man of the age, never treated him with the full ceremony due a son-in-law; their affection was like that of friends.

sentences.zh: 或人謂誇曰：「吾聞有大才者必居貴仕，子何獨在桑榆乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Suikua, 'I hear that those of great talent inevitably hold lofty office—why do you alone remain in the waning years?'
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Suikua, 'I have heard that men of great talent inevitably hold high office—why do you alone linger in your declining years?'

sentences.zh: 遂著《知命論》以釋之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote 'On Knowing Fate' to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wrote 'On Knowing Fate' to explain himself.

sentences.zh: 及卒，葬日赴會者如市。

translations.literal: When he died mourners at the funeral filled the market like a fair.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, mourners at his funeral filled the streets like a market fair.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He left no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 馮亮，字靈通，南陽人，梁平北將軍蔡道恭之甥也。

translations.literal: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, was a man of Nanyang and nephew of Liang's Pacifier of the North General Cai Daogong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, was a man of Nanyang and nephew of Cai Daogong, Liang's Pacifier of the North.

sentences.zh: 少博覽諸書，又篤好佛理。

translations.literal: In youth he read broadly in all books and was deeply devoted to Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he read widely in all books and was deeply devoted to Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 隨道恭至義陽，會中山王英平義陽，獲焉。

translations.literal: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying pacified Yiyang he was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daogong to Yiyang, and when Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying pacified Yiyang he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 英素聞其名，以禮待接。

translations.literal: Yuan Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 亮性清靜，後隱居嵩山，感英之德，以時展覲。

translations.literal: Liang's nature was pure and quiet; later he secluded himself on Mount Song, moved by Yuan Ying's virtue, and from time to time paid respectful visits.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's nature was pure and quiet; later he withdrew to Mount Song, moved by Yuan Ying's virtue, and from time to time paid him respectful visits.

sentences.zh: 英亡，亮奔赴，盡其哀慟。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ying died Liang rushed to the funeral and mourned with the utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ying died, Liang rushed to the funeral and mourned with the deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 宣武嘗召以為羽林監，領中書舍人，將令侍講《十地》諸經，固辭不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu once summoned him to serve as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and concurrently Palace Secretary, intending to have him lecture on the Dashabhumi and other sutras—he firmly refused and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu once summoned him to serve as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and concurrently Palace Secretary, intending to have him lecture on the Dashabhumi and other sutras, but he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 又欲使衣幘入見，苦求以幅巾就朝，遂不強逼。

translations.literal: They also wanted him to enter audience wearing the official cap, but he earnestly begged to attend court with only a cloth headwrap, and they did not force him further.
translations.idiomatic: They also wanted him to enter audience wearing the official cap, but he earnestly begged to attend court in a plain cloth headwrap, and they did not press him further.

sentences.zh: 還山數年，與僧禮誦為業，蔬食飲水，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Back in the mountains for several years he made chanting scripture with monks his occupation, ate vegetables and drank water, and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the mountains for several years he made chanting scripture with monks his calling, ate vegetables and drank water, and intended to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 會逆人王敞事發，連山中沙門法。

translations.literal: When the rebel Wang Chang's affair broke out it implicated the monks of the mountain monastery.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Wang Chang's affair broke out, it implicated the monks of the mountain monastery.

sentences.zh: 而亮被執赴尚書省，十餘日，詔特免雪。

translations.literal: Liang was arrested and taken to the Ministry of Justice; after more than ten days an edict specially pardoned and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was arrested and taken to the Ministry of Justice; after more than ten days an edict specially pardoned and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 亮不敢還山，遂寓居景明寺，敕給衣食及其從者數人。

translations.literal: Liang dared not return to the mountains and so lodged at Jingming Temple; the court granted food and clothing for him and several followers.
translations.idiomatic: Liang dared not return to the mountains and lodged at Jingming Temple; the court granted food and clothing for him and several followers.

sentences.zh: 後思其舊居，復還山室。

translations.literal: Later longing for his old dwelling he returned once more to his mountain cell.
translations.idiomatic: Later, longing for his old dwelling, he returned once more to his mountain cell.

sentences.zh: 亮既雅愛山水，又兼工思，結架岩林，甚得棲遊之適。

translations.literal: Since Liang both loved mountains and waters dearly and was skilled in design, he built structures among cliff forests to a very suitable degree for dwelling and wandering.
translations.idiomatic: Liang loved mountains and waters deeply and was also skilled in design; the structures he built among cliff and forest suited dwelling and wandering perfectly.

sentences.zh: 頗以此聞，宣武給其工力，令與沙門統僧暹、河南尹甄深等同視嵩山形勝之處，遂造閒居佛寺。

translations.literal: This became quite widely known; Emperor Xuanwu supplied labor so that with the Superintendent of Monks Sengxuan and Intendant of Henan Zhen Shen and others he might survey the finest places on Mount Song and there build a secluded temple.
translations.idiomatic: Word of this spread, and Emperor Xuanwu supplied labor so that Liang, together with the Superintendent of Monks Sengxuan, Intendant of Henan Zhen Shen, and others, might survey the finest sites on Mount Song and build a secluded temple there.

sentences.zh: 林泉既奇，營制又美，曲盡山居之妙。

translations.literal: The woods and springs were marvelous, the construction beautiful—the refinement of mountain dwelling was fully realized.
translations.idiomatic: The woods and springs were marvelous and the construction beautiful; the art of mountain dwelling was brought to full perfection.

sentences.zh: 亮時出京師。

translations.literal: Liang would sometimes come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang would sometimes come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年冬，因遇篤疾，宣武敕以馬輿送令還山，居嵩高道場寺，數日卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He resided at Songgao Daode Temple and died within days.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He took up residence at Songgao Daode Temple and died within days.

sentences.zh: 詔贈帛二百匹，以供凶事。

translations.literal: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 遺誡兄子綜，殮以衣蒨，左手持板，右手執《孝經》一卷，置屍磐石上，去人數里外，積十餘日，乃焚於山，灰燼處，起佛塔經藏。

translations.literal: He left instructions to his nephew Zong: enshroud the body in hemp clothes, place in the left hand a board and in the right hand one roll of the Classic of Filial Piety, set the corpse on a flat stone, withdraw several li from people, leave it more than ten days, then burn it on the mountain; where the ashes lay, raise a pagoda and scripture repository.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions to his nephew Zong: wrap the body in hemp garments, place a board in the left hand and one roll of the Classic of Filial Piety in the right, lay the corpse on a flat stone, withdraw several li from other people, leave it for more than ten days, then burn it on the mountain; where the ashes lay, raise a pagoda and a scripture repository.

sentences.zh: 初、亮以盛冬喪，連日驟雪，窮山荒澗，鳥獸饑窘，僵屍山野，無所防護。

translations.literal: At first, because Liang died in deep winter, for days snow fell fast; in the desolate ravines of the remote mountains birds and beasts were starving and distress—the corpse lay in the wild with no protection.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Liang died in deep winter, snow fell day after day; in the desolate ravines of the remote mountains birds and beasts were starving, and the corpse lay exposed in the wild with no protection.

sentences.zh: 時有壽春道人惠需，每旦往看其屍，拂去塵霰。

translations.literal: At that time the Shouyang Daoist Huixu each dawn went to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shouyang Daoist Huixu went each dawn to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.

sentences.zh: 禽蟲之跡，交橫左右，而初無侵毀。

translations.literal: Tracks of birds and insects crisscrossed left and right, yet there was never any violation or damage.
translations.idiomatic: Tracks of birds and insects crisscrossed all around, yet the body was never violated or harmed.

sentences.zh: 衣服如本，唯風蒨巾。

translations.literal: The clothing remained as before, only the hemp headwrap was wind-worn.
translations.idiomatic: The clothing remained as before, only the hemp headwrap had been worn by the wind.

sentences.zh: 又以亮識舊南方法師信大栗十枚，言期之將來十地果報，開亮手，以置把中。

translations.literal: He also placed ten large chestnuts from the southern-method teacher Xin, whom Liang had known, saying they presaged future reward of the Ten Stages—he opened Liang's hand and put them in his grasp.
translations.idiomatic: He also placed ten large chestnuts from the southern-method teacher Xin, whom Liang had known, saying they foretold future reward of the Ten Stages; he opened Liang's hand and placed them in his grasp.

sentences.zh: 經宿，乃為蟲鳥盜食，皮殼在地，而亦不傷肌體。

translations.literal: After one night they were stolen and eaten by insects and birds; the skins and shells lay on the ground, yet the flesh was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: After one night they were eaten by insects and birds; the skins and shells lay on the ground, yet the flesh was not harmed.

sentences.zh: 焚燎之日，有素霧蓊鬱，回繞其傍，自地屬天，彌朝不絕。

translations.literal: On the day of cremation a pale mist rose dense and rolled around the body from earth to sky, continuous all morning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of cremation a pale mist rose dense and rolled around the body from earth to sky, unbroken all morning.

sentences.zh: 山中道俗營助者百餘人，莫不異焉。

translations.literal: More than a hundred monks and laypeople in the mountains who assisted were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred monks and laypeople in the mountains who assisted were all astonished.

sentences.zh: 鄭修，北海人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiu was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiu was a man of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 少隱于岐南凡穀中，依岩結宇，不交世俗，雅好經史，專意玄門。

translations.literal: In youth he secluded himself in Fan Valley south of Qi, built a dwelling by the cliffs, had no dealings with the world, loved the classics and histories, and devoted himself to the dark gate.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he withdrew to Fan Valley south of Qi, built a dwelling against the cliffs, kept aloof from the world, loved the classics and histories, and devoted himself to the mysteries.

sentences.zh: 前後州將，每徵不至。

translations.literal: Prefects and generals of successive administrations summoned him but he never came.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and generals of successive administrations summoned him, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 岐州刺史魏蘭根頻遣致命，修不得已，暫出見蘭根，尋還山舍。

translations.literal: Prefect of Qi Wei Langen repeatedly sent urgent summons; Xiu had no choice but to come out briefly to see Langen, then soon returned to his mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect of Qi Wei Langen repeatedly sent urgent summons; Xiu had no choice but to come out briefly to see Langen, then soon returned to his mountain dwelling.

sentences.zh: 蘭根申表薦修，明帝詔付雍州刺史蕭寶夤訪實以聞。

translations.literal: Langen submitted a memorial recommending Xiu; Emperor Ming ordered the Prefect of Yong Province Xiao Baoyin to verify the facts and report.
translations.idiomatic: Langen submitted a memorial recommending Xiu; Emperor Ming ordered Prefect of Yong Province Xiao Baoyin to verify the facts and report back.

sentences.zh: 會寶夤作逆，事不行。

translations.literal: Baoyin rebelled and the matter came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin rebelled, and the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 崔廓，字士玄，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Kuo, styled Shixuan, was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, styled Shixuan, was a native of Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 父子元，齊燕州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Ziyuan was Military Assistant of Yan Prefecture under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziyuan was Military Assistant of Yan Prefecture under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 廓少孤貧，母賤，由是不為邦族所齒。

translations.literal: Kuo from youth was orphaned and poor; his mother was of low station, and for this reason the clan did not rank him among their number.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was orphaned and poor from youth; his mother was of low station, and for this reason the clan did not count him among their own.

sentences.zh: 初為裏佐，屢逢屈辱，於是感激，逃入山中。

translations.literal: At first he served as a village assistant and repeatedly met with humiliation; stirred by this he fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as a village assistant and was repeatedly humiliated; stirred by this, he fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 遂博覽書籍，多所通涉，山東學者皆宗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he read broadly in books and mastered many subjects; scholars east of the mountains all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: There he read widely and mastered many fields; scholars throughout the eastern provinces all looked to him as their guide.

sentences.zh: 既還鄉，不應辟命。

translations.literal: After returning to his home district he did not respond to summons to office.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he declined every summons to office.

sentences.zh: 與趙郡李士謙為忘言友，時稱崔、李。

translations.literal: He and Li Shiqian of Zhao Commandery were friends who needed no words; at the time they were called Cui and Li.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Shiqian of Zhao Commandery were friends beyond the need for words; people spoke of them together as Cui and Li.

sentences.zh: 士謙死，廓哭之慟，為之作傳，輸之秘府。

translations.literal: When Shiqian died Kuo mourned him with deep grief, wrote a biography for him, and submitted it to the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian died, Kuo mourned him with deep grief, wrote his biography, and submitted it to the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 士謙妻盧氏寡居，每家事，輒令人諮廓取定。

translations.literal: Shiqian's wife Lady Lu lived as a widow; for every household matter she would send someone to consult Kuo for a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian's widow, Lady Lu, would send someone to consult Kuo on every household matter.

sentences.zh: 廓嘗著論言刑名之理，其義甚精，文多不載。

translations.literal: Kuo once wrote a treatise on the principles of law and punishment; its meaning was very refined, but most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo once wrote a treatise on the principles of law and punishment; its argument was very fine, though most of the text is not preserved here.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，終於家。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home during the Daye era of Sui.

sentences.zh: 子賾，字祖浚，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: His son Ze, styled Zujun, at seven could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ze, styled Zujun, could compose literary pieces at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 容貌短小，有口辯。

translations.literal: His appearance was short and small, but he had eloquence in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was short in stature but gifted in debate.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，秦孝王薦之，射策高第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him and he placed at the top in the archery-and-policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him, and he placed at the top in the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 詔與諸儒定樂，授校書郎，轉協律郎。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him together with various Confucian scholars to fix the music; he was appointed Collator and later transferred to Director of Harmonization.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him, together with various Confucian scholars, to fix the court music; he was appointed Collator and later promoted to Director of Harmonization.

sentences.zh: 太常卿蘇威雅重之。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies Su Wei held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonies Su Wei held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，性至孝，水漿不入口者五日。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death; his nature was deeply filial, and for five days he took neither water nor food.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; deeply filial by nature, he took neither water nor food for five days.

sentences.zh: 後徵為河南、豫章二王侍讀，每更日來往二王之第。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to serve as Lecturer to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, each day alternating between the two princes' residences.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to serve as Lecturer to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, alternating each day between their two residences.

sentences.zh: 及河南為晉王，轉記室參軍，自此去豫章。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Henan became Prince of Jin he was transferred to Recorder of the Headquarters and from then on left Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Henan became Prince of Jin, Ze was transferred to Recorder of the Headquarters and thereafter left Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 王重之不已，遺賾書曰：

translations.literal: The prince valued him without cease and sent Ze a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: The prince valued him without cease and sent Ze a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺東苑，慕義如林，馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。

translations.literal: In former times the Western Capital of Han and the founding of Liang's state, the Level Terrace and Eastern Park drew men of virtue like a forest; Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Feathered Cavalry, Mei Sheng gave up his governorship of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, at the Western Capital of Han and when Liang founded its state, the Level Terrace and Eastern Park drew men of virtue like a forest; Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Feathered Cavalry, and Mei Sheng gave up his governorship of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗竊怪之：何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？

translations.literal: Whenever I read the histories I have privately wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger in princely residences?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the histories I have privately wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger in princely residences?

sentences.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。

translations.literal: Looking from the present back to antiquity, I now understand their lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: Looking from the present back to antiquity, I now understand their lofty intent.

sentences.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Those two men—were they merely acting in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Those two men were not acting in vain!

sentences.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似陟蒙山；

translations.literal: You, sir, are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing the deep to reach the far; compared with the three baskets of a Han minister, it is like ascending Mount Meng;
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing the deep to reach the far; compared with the three baskets of a Han minister, it is like ascending Mount Meng;

sentences.zh: 對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。

translations.literal: faced with the five cartloads of a Liang chancellor, it is like swallowing Lake Yunmeng.
translations.idiomatic: faced with the five cartloads of a Liang chancellor, it is like swallowing Lake Yunmeng whole.

sentences.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。

translations.literal: My elder brother cherishes the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring and loving them without weariness; he first built a palace for Guo Kui and always kept the wine of Mu Sheng ready.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother cherishes the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring them without weariness; he first built a palace for Guo Kui and always kept the wine of Mu Sheng ready.

sentences.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河。

translations.literal: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 地方七百，牢籠曲阜；

translations.literal: His territory spans seven hundred li and encloses Qufu;
translations.idiomatic: His territory spans seven hundred li and encloses Qufu;

sentences.zh: 城兼七十，包舉臨淄。

translations.literal: his cities number seventy and embrace Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: his cities number seventy and embrace Linzi.

sentences.zh: 大啟南陽，方開東閤。

translations.literal: Greatly opening Nanyang, he is just now opening the Eastern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly opening Nanyang, he is just now opening the Eastern Gate to welcome guests.

sentences.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。

translations.literal: I imagine you will ride beneath a flying canopy, trail a long robe, recline on a tortoiseshell mat, step in pearl slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's lofty grace, and compose on the pool bamboo's elegant clusters.
translations.idiomatic: I imagine you will ride beneath a flying canopy, trail a long robe, recline on a tortoiseshell mat, step in pearl slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's lofty grace, and compose verses on the pool bamboo's elegant clusters.

sentences.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Your lofty dignity is like that, your elegant spirit like this—how fortunate, how fortunate! What joy could equal it!
translations.idiomatic: Your lofty dignity is like that, your elegant spirit like this—how fortunate, how fortunate! What joy could equal it!

sentences.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖；

translations.literal: Looking up to the capital, I think of Dezuo;
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to the capital, I think of Dezuo;

sentences.zh: 才謝天人，多慚子建。

translations.literal: in talent I fall short of heaven and man, and am much ashamed before Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: in talent I fall short of heaven and man, and am much ashamed before Zijian.

sentences.zh: 書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。

translations.literal: A letter cannot exhaust my meaning; why wait for more words?
translations.idiomatic: A letter cannot exhaust my meaning; why wait for more words?

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：

translations.literal: Ze replied:
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied:

sentences.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。

translations.literal: Yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was beyond the ordinary, and my spirit lost itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was beyond the ordinary, and my spirit was overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 若乃理高《象系》，管輅思而不解；

translations.literal: As for reasoning that surpasses the Image and Attachment of the Changes, even Guan Lu would ponder without understanding;
translations.idiomatic: As for reasoning that surpasses the Image and Attachment of the Changes, even Guan Lu would ponder without understanding;

sentences.zh: 事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。

translations.literal: matters rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated yet could not exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: matters rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated them yet could not exhaust them.

sentences.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。

translations.literal: As for the five colors harmonizing, the eight tones gathering in abundance—phoenix song is insufficient as a metaphor, dragon pattern has no equal.
translations.idiomatic: As for the five colors harmonizing and the eight tones gathering in abundance—phoenix song is insufficient as a metaphor, and dragon pattern has no equal.

sentences.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚；

translations.literal: Wu Zha's discourse on the Zhou Eulogies—how could it fully praise you;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zha's discourse on the Zhou Eulogies—how could it fully praise you;

sentences.zh: 郢客之奏《陽春》，誰能赴節？

translations.literal: the Ying guest's performance of 'Spring Sun'—who could match the measure?
translations.idiomatic: the Ying guest's performance of 'Spring Sun'—who could match the measure?

sentences.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道邁于東平，文藝高於北海。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Prince, endowed with the moisture of the Heavenly Ford and inheriting radiance from Sun-View Peak, surpasses the Prince of Dongping in refined learning and rises above the Prince of Beihai in literary art.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Prince, endowed with the moisture of the Heavenly Ford and inheriting radiance from Sun-View Peak, surpasses the Prince of Dongping in refined learning and rises above the Prince of Beihai in literary art.

sentences.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。

translations.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。

translations.literal: Your fame rises at the Rooster Tree, your beauty spreads at the Egret Pool; gazing at my clear dust, the path between us is far and still.
translations.idiomatic: Your fame rises at the Rooster Tree, your beauty spreads at the Egret Pool; gazing at my humble dust, the path between us is far and still.

sentences.zh: 祖浚燕南贅客，河朔惰游，本無意于希顏，豈有心于慕藺。

translations.literal: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of Yan, an idle wanderer of the northern Yellow River region; I never intended to emulate Yan Hui, nor had any mind to admire Lin Xiangru.
translations.idiomatic: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of Yan, an idle wanderer of the northern Yellow River region; I never intended to emulate Yan Hui, nor had any mind to admire Lin Xiangru.

sentences.zh: 未嘗聚螢映雪，懸頭刺股。

translations.literal: I have never gathered fireflies to read by snowlight, nor hung my head and pricked my thigh in study.
translations.idiomatic: I have never gathered fireflies to read by snowlight, nor hung my head and pricked my thigh in study.

sentences.zh: 讀《論》唯取一篇，披《莊》不過盈尺。

translations.literal: Reading the Analects I take only one chapter; opening the Zhuangzi I read no more than a foot's length.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Analects I take only one chapter; opening the Zhuangzi I read no more than a foot's length.

sentences.zh: 況復桑榆漸暮，藜藿屢空，舉燭無成，穿楊盡棄。

translations.literal: Moreover my mulberry and elm years draw toward evening, my wild greens are often empty, raising the candle yields no success, and shooting through the willow is wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my mulberry-and-elm years draw toward evening, my wild greens are often empty, raising the candle yields no success, and shooting through the willow is wholly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 但以燕求馬首，薛養雞鳴，謬齒鴻儀，虛班驥ＩＺ。

translations.literal: Yet like Yan seeking the horse's head, or Xue raising the cock's crow, I wrongly take rank among the grand rites and falsely occupy a place among fine steeds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet like Yan seeking the horse's head, or Xue raising the cock's crow, I wrongly take rank among the grand rites and falsely occupy a place among fine steeds.

sentences.zh: 挾太山而超海，比報德而非難；

translations.literal: To clasp Mount Tai and leap over the sea—compared with repaying your kindness this would not be hard;
translations.idiomatic: To clasp Mount Tai and leap over the sea—compared with repaying your kindness this would not be hard;

sentences.zh: 堙昆侖以為池，匹酬恩而反易。

translations.literal: to dam Mount Kunlun and make it a pool—matching your grace in return would instead be easy.
translations.idiomatic: to dam Mount Kunlun and make it a pool—matching your grace in return would instead be easy.

sentences.zh: 忽屬周桐錫瑞，唐水承家，門有將相，樹宜桃李。

translations.literal: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia received its auspice, the Tang waters inherited the house; your gate has generals and ministers, your tree is fit for peaches and plums.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia received its auspice, the Tang waters inherited the house; your gate has generals and ministers, and your tree is fit for peaches and plums.

sentences.zh: 真龍將下，誰好有名；

translations.literal: When the true dragon is about to descend, who would care to be famous;
translations.idiomatic: When the true dragon is about to descend, who would care to be famous;

sentences.zh: 濫吹先逃，何須別聽。

translations.literal: the incompetent flute-player should flee first—why need another hearing?
translations.idiomatic: the incompetent flute-player should flee first—why need another hearing?

sentences.zh: 但慈旨抑揚，損上益下，江海所以稱王，丘陵為之不逮。

translations.literal: Yet your gracious intent lowers the high and raises the low; it is for this that rivers and seas are called kings, and hills and mounds cannot match them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your gracious intent lowers the high and raises the low; it is for this that rivers and seas are called kings, and hills and mounds cannot match them.

sentences.zh: 曹植儻豫聞高論，則不殞令名；

translations.literal: If Cao Zhi by chance heard your lofty discourse, his fine name would not perish;
translations.idiomatic: If Cao Zhi by chance heard your lofty discourse, his fine name would not perish;

sentences.zh: 楊脩若竊在下風，亦詎虧淳德。

translations.literal: if Yang Xiu secretly stood in your lee, his pure virtue would likewise not be diminished.
translations.idiomatic: if Yang Xiu secretly stood in your lee, his pure virtue would likewise not be diminished.

sentences.zh: 無任荷戴之至，謹奉啟以聞。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the fullness of my gratitude, I respectfully submit this letter to inform you.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the fullness of my gratitude, I respectfully submit this letter to inform you.

sentences.zh: 豫章得書，齎米五十石，並衣服、錢帛。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang received his letter and sent fifty piculs of rice, along with clothing, money, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang received his letter and sent fifty piculs of rice, along with clothing, money, and silks.

sentences.zh: 時晉邸文翰，多成其手。

translations.literal: At the time the documents of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the documents of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his own hand.

sentences.zh: 王入東宮，除太子齋帥，俄兼舍人。

translations.literal: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Master of the Crown Prince's Fast, and soon also served as Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Master of the Crown Prince's Fast, and soon also served as Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及元德太子薨，以疾歸於家。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yuande died, he returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yuande died, he returned home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 後征起居舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Imperial Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned as Imperial Diarist.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，從駕汾陽宮，次河陽鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye he accompanied the imperial procession to Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daye he accompanied the imperial procession to Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 藍田令王曇于藍田山得一玉人，長三四寸，著大領衣，冠幘。

translations.literal: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, obtained a jade figure on Mount Lantian, three or four inches tall, wearing a broad-collared robe and a cap with headwrap.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, obtained a jade figure on Mount Lantian, three or four inches tall, wearing a broad-collared robe and a cap with headwrap.

sentences.zh: 奏之。

translations.literal: He memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: He reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔問群臣，莫有識者。

translations.literal: An edict asked the assembled ministers, but none recognized it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict asked the assembled ministers, but none could identify it.

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：「謹案：漢文帝已前，未有冠幘，即是文帝以來所制也。

translations.literal: Ze replied: 'I respectfully consider: before Emperor Wen of Han there were no caps with headwraps; this must have been made from Emperor Wen's time onward.
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied: 'I respectfully consider: before Emperor Wen of Han there were no caps with headwraps; this must have been made from Emperor Wen's time onward.

sentences.zh: 臣見魏大司農盧元明撰《嵩高山廟記》云：『有神人，以玉為形，像長數寸，或出或隱，出則令世延長。』

translations.literal: Your subject has seen the Record of the Song Mountain Temple written by Lu Yuanming, Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, which says: "There is a divine being in the form of jade, a figure several inches long, who sometimes appears and sometimes hides; when he appears the age is prolonged."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has seen the Record of the Song Mountain Temple written by Lu Yuanming, Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, which says: "There is a divine being in the form of jade, a figure several inches long, who sometimes appears and sometimes hides; when he appears the age is prolonged."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，應天順人，定鼎嵩、雒，嶽神自見，臣敢稱慶。」

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and following the people, has fixed the tripod at Song and Luo; the mountain god has revealed himself, and your subject dares to offer congratulations.'
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and following the people, has fixed the tripod at Song and Luo; the mountain god has revealed himself, and your subject dares to offer congratulations.'

sentences.zh: 因再拜，百官畢賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed twice, and all the officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he bowed twice, and all the officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 天子大悅，賜縑二百匹。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 從駕往太山，詔問賾曰：「何處有羊腸阪？」

translations.literal: Accompanying the procession to Mount Tai, an edict asked Ze: 'Where is Yangchang Slope?'
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the procession to Mount Tai, the emperor asked Ze: 'Where is Yangchang Slope?'

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：「臣案《漢書·地理志》，上党壺關縣有羊腸阪。」

translations.literal: Ze replied: 'Your subject finds in the Geography Monograph of the Book of Han that Yangchang Slope is in Huguan County, Shangdang.'
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied: 'Your subject finds in the Geography Monograph of the Book of Han that Yangchang Slope is in Huguan County, Shangdang.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不是。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'That is not it.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'That is not it.'

sentences.zh: 又答曰：「臣案皇甫士安撰《地書》，云太原北九十里，有羊腸阪。」

translations.literal: He replied again: 'Your subject finds in the Geography written by Huangfu Shi'an that ninety li north of Taiyuan there is a Yangchang Slope.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied again: 'Your subject finds in the Geography written by Huangfu Shi'an that ninety li north of Taiyuan there is a Yangchang Slope.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'That is it.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'That is it.'

sentences.zh: 因謂牛弘曰：「崔祖浚所謂問一知二。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: 'This is what Cui Zujun means by asking one and knowing two.'
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: 'This is what Cui Zujun means by asking one and knowing two.'

sentences.zh: 五年，受詔與諸儒撰《區宇圖志》二百五十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he received an edict to compile with various Confucian scholars the Gazetteer of the Realm in two hundred fifty volumes, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received an edict to compile, with various Confucian scholars, the Gazetteer of the Realm in two hundred fifty volumes, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝不善之，更令虞世基、許善心演為六百卷。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shansin to expand it into six hundred volumes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shansin to expand it into six hundred volumes.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's death, but soon was recalled and ordered to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father, but was soon recalled and ordered to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，授鷹揚長史。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Soaring Hawk Command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Soaring Hawk Command.

sentences.zh: 置遼東郡縣名，皆賾之議也。

translations.literal: The names of the commanderies and counties established in Liaodong were all Ze's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The names of the commanderies and counties established in Liaodong were all Ze's proposals.

sentences.zh: 奉詔作《東征記》。

translations.literal: He received an edict to compose the Record of the Eastern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He received an edict to compose the Record of the Eastern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 九年，除越王長史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 于時山東盜賊蜂起，帝令撫慰高陽、襄國，歸首者八百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose like bees in the eastern provinces; the emperor ordered him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and more than eight hundred surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits rose like bees in the eastern provinces; the emperor ordered him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and more than eight hundred surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從駕江都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑帝也，引為著作郎，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji assassinated the emperor he was appointed Compiler, but Ze pleaded illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji assassinated the emperor, Ze was appointed Compiler, but he pleaded illness and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 在路發疾，卒于彭城，年六十九。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he fell ill and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賾與河南元善、河東柳䛒、太原王劭、吳興姚察、琅琊諸葛潁、信都劉焯、河間劉炫相善，每因休假，清談竟日。

translations.literal: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.

sentences.zh: 所著詞、賦、碑、志十餘萬言，撰《洽聞志》七卷，《八代四科志》三十卷。

translations.literal: His writings in rhapsodies, fu, stele inscriptions, and records totaled more than one hundred thousand characters; he compiled the Record of Broad Learning in seven volumes and the Record of Four Categories through Eight Dynasties in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: His writings in rhapsodies, fu, stele inscriptions, and records totaled more than one hundred thousand characters; he compiled the Record of Broad Learning in seven volumes and the Record of Four Categories through Eight Dynasties in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 未及施行，江都傾覆，咸為煨燼。

translations.literal: Before they could be put into effect Jiangdu fell, and all were reduced to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could be put into effect Jiangdu fell, and all were reduced to ashes.

sentences.zh: 徐則，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ze was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ze was a native of Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 幼沈靜，寡嗜欲，受業于周弘正，善三玄，精於論議，聲擅都邑。

translations.literal: From youth he was quiet and reserved, with few desires; he studied under Zhou Hongzheng, was skilled in the Three Mysteries, excelled in disputation, and his fame filled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quiet and reserved, with few desires; he studied under Zhou Hongzheng, was skilled in the Three Mysteries, excelled in disputation, and his fame filled the capital.

sentences.zh: 則歎曰：「名者實之賓，吾其為賓乎！」

translations.literal: Ze sighed and said: 'Fame is the guest of reality—am I to be the guest!'
translations.idiomatic: Ze sighed and said: 'Fame is the guest of reality—am I to be the guest!'

sentences.zh: 遂懷棲隱之操，杖策入縉雲山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he embraced the resolve to dwell in seclusion, took staff in hand, and entered Mount Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he embraced the resolve to dwell in seclusion, took staff in hand, and entered Mount Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 後學者數百人苦請教授，則謝而遣之。

translations.literal: Later several hundred students earnestly begged him to teach, but Ze declined and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Later several hundred students earnestly begged him to teach, but Ze declined and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 不娶妻，常服巾褐。

translations.literal: He did not marry and always wore a cloth cap and hemp robe.
translations.idiomatic: He did not marry and always wore a cloth cap and hemp robe.

sentences.zh: 陳太建中，應召來憩於至真觀。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era of Chen he answered a summons and came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era of Chen he answered a summons and came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 期月，又辭入天台山。

translations.literal: After a month he again took leave and entered Mount Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he again took leave and entered Mount Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 因絕粒養性，所資唯松水而已，雖隆冬冱寒，不服綿絮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abstained from grain to nurture his nature; his sole sustenance was pine water; even in the deep cold of midwinter he wore no cotton padding.
translations.idiomatic: There he abstained from grain to nurture his nature; his sole sustenance was pine water; even in the deep cold of midwinter he wore no cotton padding.

sentences.zh: 太傅徐陵為之刊山立頌。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Xu Ling carved a mountain inscription and erected a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xu Ling carved a mountain inscription and erected a eulogy for him.

sentences.zh: 初在縉雲山，太極真人徐君降之曰：「汝年出八十，當為王者師，然後得道也。」

translations.literal: When he was first on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected One of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, descended to him and said: 'When your years pass eighty you will become teacher to a king, and only then attain the Way.'
translations.idiomatic: When he was first on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected One of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, descended to him and said: 'When your years pass eighty you will become teacher to a king, and only then attain the Way.'

sentences.zh: 晉王廣鎮揚州，聞其名，手書召之曰：「夫道得眾妙，法體自然，包涵二儀，混成萬物，人能弘道，道不虛行。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang held Yangzhou and, hearing his name, personally wrote to summon him: 'The Way obtains the myriad subtleties; its law embodies nature, embraces the two principles, and blends to form the ten thousand things. Man can expand the Way, and the Way does not move in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang held Yangzhou and, hearing his name, personally wrote to summon him: 'The Way obtains the myriad subtleties; its law embodies nature, embraces the two principles, and blends to form the ten thousand things. Man can expand the Way, and the Way does not move in vain.

sentences.zh: 先生履德養空，宗玄齊物，深曉義理，頗味法門。

translations.literal: You, sir, tread virtue and nurture emptiness, take the dark as your standard and align with things, deeply understand principle and reason, and have tasted the gates of the Law.
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, tread virtue and nurture emptiness, take the dark as your standard and align with things, deeply understand principle and reason, and have tasted the gates of the Law.

sentences.zh: 悅性沖玄，恬神虛白，餐松餌術，棲息煙霞。

translations.literal: Your nature delights in pure mystery, your spirit is tranquil and empty-white; you dine on pine and take elixirs, dwelling amid mist and rosy clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Your nature delights in pure mystery, your spirit is tranquil and empty-white; you dine on pine and take elixirs, dwelling amid mist and rosy clouds.

sentences.zh: 望赤城而待風雲，遊玉堂而駕龍鳳。

translations.literal: Gazing toward Red Wall to await wind and clouds, roaming the Jade Hall and driving dragon and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward Red Wall to await wind and clouds, roaming the Jade Hall and driving dragon and phoenix.

sentences.zh: 雖復藏名台嶽，猶且騰實江、淮。

translations.literal: Though you again conceal your name on terrace and peak, your substance still rises along the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Though you again conceal your name on terrace and peak, your substance still rises along the Yangtze and Huai.

sentences.zh: 藉甚嘉猷，有勞寤寐。

translations.literal: Your excellent counsel is greatly renowned and has long occupied my waking and sleeping thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Your excellent counsel is greatly renowned and has long occupied my waking and sleeping thoughts.

sentences.zh: 欽承素道，久積虛襟，側席幽人，夢想岩穴。

translations.literal: I respectfully receive your pure Way, long accumulated in my empty breast; I sit askance for the recluse and dream of mountain caves.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully receive your pure Way, long held in my open heart; I sit askance for the recluse and dream of mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 霜風已冷，海氣將寒，偃息茂林，道體休悆。

translations.literal: The frost wind is already cold and the sea air will soon turn chill; rest at ease in the lush forest and let your Way-body find repose.
translations.idiomatic: The frost wind is already cold and the sea air will soon turn chill; rest at ease in the lush forest and let your Way-body find repose.

sentences.zh: 昔商山四皓，輕舉漢庭；

translations.literal: In former times the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang lightly entered the Han court;
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang lightly entered the Han court;

sentences.zh: 淮南八公，來儀籓邸。

translations.literal: the Eight Worthies of Huainan came as guests to a princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: the Eight Worthies of Huainan came as guests to a princely residence.

sentences.zh: 古今雖異，山谷不殊。

translations.literal: Though ancient and modern differ, mountains and valleys are not unlike.
translations.idiomatic: Though ancient and modern differ, mountains and valleys are not unlike.

sentences.zh: 市朝之隱，前賢已說。

translations.literal: Reclusion within the marketplace and court—former worthies have already spoken of it.
translations.idiomatic: Reclusion within the marketplace and court—former worthies have already spoken of it.

sentences.zh: 導凡述聖。

translations.literal: To guide the common and expound the sage—
translations.idiomatic: To guide the common and expound the sage—

sentences.zh: 非先生而誰？

translations.literal: if not you, sir, then who?
translations.idiomatic: if not you, sir, then who?

sentences.zh: 故遣使人，往彼延請，想無勞東帛，賁然來思，不待蒲輪，去彼空穀。

translations.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to go there and invite you; I trust you need not be urged with silk gifts but will come with radiant intent, and need not wait for rush-wheeled carriages to leave that empty valley.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I send an envoy to invite you; I trust you need not be urged with silk gifts but will come with radiant intent, and need not wait for rush-wheeled carriages to leave that empty valley.

sentences.zh: 希能屈己，佇望披云。」

translations.literal: I hope you can humble yourself; I wait in expectation to part the clouds.'
translations.idiomatic: I hope you can humble yourself; I wait in expectation to part the clouds.'

sentences.zh: 則謂門人曰：「吾今年八十一，王來召我，徐君之旨，信而不征。」

translations.literal: Ze said to his disciples: 'I am eighty-one this year; the prince has come to summon me—Lord Xu's prophecy is trustworthy and not false.'
translations.idiomatic: Ze said to his disciples: 'I am eighty-one this year; the prince has come to summon me—Lord Xu's prophecy is trustworthy and not false.'

sentences.zh: 於是遂詣揚州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he went to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王將請受道法，則辭以時日不便。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way, but Ze declined on the grounds that the time was not suitable.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way, but Ze declined on the grounds that the time was not suitable.

sentences.zh: 其後夕中，命待者取香火，如平常朝禮之儀，至於五更而死。

translations.literal: That evening he ordered his attendants to fetch incense and fire and perform the usual morning ritual; by the fifth watch he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he ordered his attendants to fetch incense and fire and perform the usual morning ritual; by the fifth watch he was dead.

sentences.zh: 支體柔弱如生，停留數旬，顏色不變。

translations.literal: His limbs were soft as in life; he remained for several tens of days and his complexion did not change.
translations.idiomatic: His limbs were soft as in life; he remained for several tens of days and his complexion did not change.

sentences.zh: 晉王下書曰：「天台真隱東海徐先生，虛確居宗，沖玄成德，齊物處外，檢行安身。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin issued a letter: 'The true recluse of Mount Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai, takes emptiness and certainty as his standard, forms virtue through pure mystery, aligns with things while standing apart, and restrains conduct to secure his person.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin issued a letter: 'The true recluse of Mount Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai, takes emptiness and certainty as his standard, forms virtue through pure mystery, aligns with things while standing apart, and restrains conduct to secure his person.

sentences.zh: 草褐蒲衣，餐松餌朮，棲隱靈岳，五十餘年。

translations.literal: In hemp robe and rush garment he dined on pine and took atractylodes, dwelling in seclusion on the numinous peak for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: In hemp robe and rush garment he dined on pine and took atractylodes, dwelling in seclusion on the numinous peak for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 卓矣仙才，飄然騰氣，千尋萬頃，莫測其涯。

translations.literal: Transcendent was his immortal talent, soaring and ethereal; a thousand fathoms and ten thousand acres—none could measure his bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Transcendent was his immortal talent, soaring and ethereal; a thousand fathoms and ten thousand acres—none could measure his bounds.

sentences.zh: 寡人欽承道風，久餐德素，頻遣使乎，遠此延屈，冀得虔受上法，式建良緣。

translations.literal: I have long admired his Way-wind and nourished myself on his pure virtue, repeatedly sending envoys to invite him from afar, hoping to receive the higher Law devoutly and establish a fine bond.
translations.idiomatic: I have long admired his Way-wind and nourished myself on his pure virtue, repeatedly sending envoys to invite him from afar, hoping to receive the higher Law devoutly and establish a fine bond.

sentences.zh: 至止甫爾，未淹旬日，厭塵羽化，反真靈府。

translations.literal: He had just arrived and not yet passed ten days when, weary of the dust, he transformed by feather and returned to the numinous realm.
translations.idiomatic: He had just arrived and not yet passed ten days when, weary of the dust, he transformed by feather and returned to the numinous realm.

sentences.zh: 身體柔軟，顏色不變，經方所謂屍解地仙者哉。

translations.literal: His body was soft and his complexion unchanged—is this not what the scriptures call a corpse-dissolving earthly immortal?
translations.idiomatic: His body was soft and his complexion unchanged—is this not what the scriptures call a corpse-dissolving earthly immortal?

sentences.zh: 誠復師禮未申，而心許有在，雖忘怛化，猶愴於懷。

translations.literal: Truly the rites of master and disciple were not yet performed, yet a promise of the heart remained; though he forgot sorrow in transformation, grief still lodges in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the rites of master and disciple were not yet performed, yet a promise of the heart remained; though he forgot sorrow in transformation, grief still lodges in my breast.

sentences.zh: 喪事所資，隨須供給。

translations.literal: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed.

sentences.zh: 霓裳羽蓋，既且騰雲；

translations.literal: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies have already risen on clouds;
translations.idiomatic: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies have already risen on clouds;

sentences.zh: 空槨餘衣，詎藉墳壟？

translations.literal: an empty coffin and leftover garments—why rely on mound and tomb?
translations.idiomatic: an empty coffin and leftover garments—why rely on mound and tomb?

sentences.zh: 但杖舄在爾，可同俗法。

translations.literal: Only the staff and shoes remain with you; you may follow the common custom.
translations.idiomatic: Only the staff and shoes remain with you; you may follow the common custom.

sentences.zh: 宜遣使人，送還天台定葬。」

translations.literal: You should send envoys to return him to Mount Tiantai for burial.'
translations.idiomatic: You should send envoys to return him to Mount Tiantai for burial.'

sentences.zh: 是時，自江都至天台，在道多見則徒步，云得放還。

translations.literal: At that time, from Jiangdu to Mount Tiantai, many on the road saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, from Jiangdu to Mount Tiantai, many on the road saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.

sentences.zh: 至其舊居，取經書道法，分遣弟子，仍令淨掃一房，曰：「若有客至，宜延之於此。」

translations.literal: When he reached his old dwelling he took out scriptures and Daoist methods, distributed them among his disciples, and ordered a room swept clean, saying: 'If guests come, they should be received here.'
translations.idiomatic: When he reached his old dwelling he took out scriptures and Daoist methods, distributed them among his disciples, and ordered a room swept clean, saying: 'If guests come, they should be received here.'

sentences.zh: 然後跨石梁而去，不知所之。

translations.literal: Then he crossed the stone bridge and departed, and no one knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: Then he crossed the stone bridge and departed, and no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 須臾屍柩至，知其靈化，時年八十二。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the coffin arrived; they knew he had undergone spiritual transformation; he was then eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the coffin arrived; they knew he had undergone spiritual transformation; he was then eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞而益異之，賵物千段，遣畫工圖其狀，令柳{巧言}為之贊。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Yan to compose a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Yan to compose a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 時有建安宋玉泉、會稽孔道茂、丹陽王遠知等，亦行辟穀道，以松水自給，皆為煬帝所重。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, and Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, who likewise practiced the Way of grain abstinence and sustained themselves on pine water—all were esteemed by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were also Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, and Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, who likewise practiced the Way of grain abstinence and sustained themselves on pine water—all were esteemed by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 張文詡

translations.literal: Zhang Wenxu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenxu

sentences.zh: 張文詡，河東人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenxu was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenxu was a man of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父琚，開皇中，為洹水令，以清正聞。

translations.literal: His father Ju, during Kaihuang, served as magistrate of Huanshui and was known for integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju, during Kaihuang, served as magistrate of Huanshui and was known for integrity and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 文詡博覽群書，特精《三禮》。

translations.literal: Wenxu read broadly in all books and was especially expert in the Three Rituals.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu read broadly in all books and was especially expert in the Three Rituals.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝方引天下名儒碩學之士，文詡時游太學，博士房暉遠等莫不推伏之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui was then gathering renowned Confucian scholars and eminent learned men from throughout the realm; Wenxu was then studying at the Imperial Academy, and Erudites such as Fang Huiyuan all deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui was then gathering renowned Confucian scholars and eminent learned men from throughout the realm; Wenxu was studying at the Imperial Academy, and Erudites such as Fang Huiyuan all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 書侍御史皇甫誕，一時朝彥，恆執弟子之禮，以所乘馬就學邀屈。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Huangfu Dan, a leading figure of the court, always performed the rites of a disciple and used the horse he rode to invite Wenxu to study.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Huangfu Dan, a leading figure of the court, always performed the rites of a disciple and used the horse he rode to invite Wenxu to study.

sentences.zh: 文詡遂每牽馬步進，意在不因人自致也。

translations.literal: Wenxu therefore each time led the horse and walked on foot, intending not to advance himself through others.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu therefore each time led the horse and walked on foot, intending not to advance himself through others.

sentences.zh: 右僕射蘇威聞而召之，與語大悅，勸令從官，文詡固辭。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Su Wei heard of him and summoned him; after conversing he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office, but Wenxu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Su Wei heard of him and summoned him; after conversing he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office, but Wenxu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，學廢，文詡策杖而歸，灌園為業。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou the academy was abolished; Wenxu returned leaning on a staff and made watering gardens his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Renshou the academy was abolished; Wenxu returned leaning on a staff and made watering gardens his occupation.

sentences.zh: 州郡頻舉，皆不應命。

translations.literal: Prefectures and commanderies repeatedly recommended him, but he never answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and commanderies repeatedly recommended him, but he never answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 每以德化人，鄉黨頗移風俗。

translations.literal: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and neighborhood gradually changed their customs.
translations.idiomatic: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and neighborhood gradually changed their customs.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人夜中竊刈其麥者，見而避之。

translations.literal: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and stepped aside.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and stepped aside.

sentences.zh: 盜因感悟，棄麥而謝。

translations.literal: The thief was moved by this, abandoned the wheat, and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was moved by this, abandoned the wheat, and apologized.

sentences.zh: 文詡慰諭之，自誓不言，固令持去。

translations.literal: Wenxu comforted and instructed him, swore he would not speak of it, and firmly told him to take the wheat away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu comforted and instructed him, swore he would not speak of it, and firmly told him to take the wheat away.

sentences.zh: 經數年，盜者向鄉人說之，始為遠近所悉。

translations.literal: After several years the thief told fellow villagers, and only then did those near and far come to know of it.
