translations.idiomatic: After several years the thief told fellow villagers, and only then did those near and far come to know of it.

sentences.zh: 鄰家築牆，心有不直，文詡因毀舊堵以應之。

translations.literal: When a neighbor built a wall with an inward bend in his heart, Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to accommodate him.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor built a wall that encroached inward, Wenxu tore down his old wall to accommodate him.

sentences.zh: 文詡常有腰疾，會醫者自言善禁，文詡令禁之，遂為刀所傷，至於頓伏床枕。

translations.literal: Wenxu often suffered from a waist ailment; once a physician claimed skill in incantation-healing, and Wenxu had him perform it, but was wounded by a knife and collapsed on bed and pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu often suffered from a waist ailment; once a physician claimed skill in incantation-healing, and Wenxu had him perform it, but was wounded by a knife and collapsed on bed and pillow.

sentences.zh: 醫者叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 文詡遽遣之，因為隱，謂妻子曰：「吾昨風眩，落坑所致。」

translations.literal: Wenxu at once sent him away and concealed the matter, telling his wife and children: 'I had a dizzy spell yesterday and fell into a pit.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu at once sent him away and concealed the matter, telling his wife and children: 'I had a dizzy spell yesterday and fell into a pit.'

sentences.zh: 其掩人短，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His concealing others' faults was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His way of concealing others' faults was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 州縣以其貧素，將加賑恤，輒辭不受。

translations.literal: Because he was poor and plain, prefectures and counties were about to grant relief, but he always declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was poor and plain, prefectures and counties were about to grant relief, but he always declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 嘗閒居無事，從容歎曰：「老冉冉而將至，恐修名之不立！」

translations.literal: Once, idle at home with nothing to do, he sighed at ease and said: 'Old age slowly approaches—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!'
translations.idiomatic: Once, idle at home with nothing to do, he sighed at ease and said: 'Old age slowly approaches—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!'

sentences.zh: 以如意擊幾自樂，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫、原憲焉。

translations.literal: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

sentences.zh: 終於家，鄉人為立碑頌，號曰張先生。

translations.literal: He died at home; fellow villagers erected a stele in his praise and called him Master Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home; fellow villagers erected a stele in his praise and called him Master Zhang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古之所謂隱逸者，非伏其身而不見也，非閉其言而不出也，非藏其智而不發也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: What the ancients called recluses was not hiding the body so it would not be seen, not closing the words so they would not be spoken, not concealing wisdom so it would not be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: What the ancients called recluses was not hiding the body so it would not be seen, not closing the words so they would not be spoken, not concealing wisdom so it would not be deployed.

sentences.zh: 蓋以恬淡為心，不皦不昧，安時處順，與物無私者也。

translations.literal: Rather, they took tranquil simplicity as their heart, neither glaring nor dim, adapting to the times and following what is fitting, without private attachment to things.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, they took tranquil simplicity as their heart, neither glaring nor dim, adapting to the times and following what is fitting, without private attachment to things.

sentences.zh: 眭誇忘懷纓冕，畢志丘園，或隱不違親，貞不絕俗；

translations.literal: Suikua forgot official rank and cap, fulfilled his purpose in hills and gardens, concealing himself without violating kinship, remaining pure without cutting off the world;
translations.idiomatic: Suikua forgot official rank and cap, fulfilled his purpose in hills and gardens, concealing himself without violating kinship, remaining pure without cutting off the world;

sentences.zh: 或不教而勸，虛往實歸，非有自然純德，其孰能至此？

translations.literal: or teaching without instruction and sending empty but receiving full—without natural pure virtue, who could reach this?
translations.idiomatic: or teaching without instruction and sending empty but receiving full—without natural pure virtue, who could reach this?

sentences.zh: 然文詡見傷無慍，徐則志在沈冥，不可親疏，莫能貴賤，皆可謂抱樸之士矣。

translations.literal: Yet Wenxu, though injured, was without anger; Xu Ze's intent lay in deep obscurity—neither closeness nor distance, neither nobility nor baseness could affect him; all may be called men who embraced simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wenxu, though injured, was without anger; Xu Ze's intent lay in deep obscurity—neither closeness nor distance, neither nobility nor baseness could affect him; all may be called men who embraced simplicity.

sentences.zh: 崔廓感於屈辱，遂以肥遁見稱；

translations.literal: Cui Kuo, stirred by humiliation, came to be praised for his deep withdrawal;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, stirred by humiliation, came to be praised for his deep withdrawal;

sentences.zh: 祖浚文籍之美，足以克隆堂構。

translations.literal: Zujun's excellence in letters was sufficient to continue the hall and framework of his house.
translations.idiomatic: Zujun's excellence in letters was sufficient to continue the hall and framework of his house.

sentences.zh: 父子雖動靜殊方，其于成名一也，美哉！

translations.literal: Though father and son differed in movement and stillness, in achieving fame they were one—how fine!
translations.idiomatic: Though father and son differed in movement and stillness, in achieving fame they were one—how fine!
